evidence: security-audit.yml:32-33 writes SOURCE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) to $GITHUB_ENV, which is visible to later steps; the dispatch step (34-39) does not override it. security_advisories.py:361 reads os.environ.get('SOURCE_SHA','') so a missing value is ''. dispatch() line 102 calls revision(sha), which uses SHA.fullmatch (40 hex, lines 24, 82-84) and raises AuditError('Invalid revision') on ''. Absolute-style input: unset SOURCE_SHA gives '' which fails the match.

security-audit.yml:38 sets LOOKBACK_DAYS: ${{ inputs.lookback_days || '7' }}; the input is declared only under workflow_dispatch (lines 8-13), so on schedule the inputs context property is empty and the expression falls back to '7'. security_advisories.py:87-90 lookback() uses fullmatch [0-9]{1,2} and requires 1<=int<=90, raising AuditError otherwise (no defaulting), so out-of-range manual input fails the run. Not traced: the call site of lookback() beyond dispatch() at line 101.

dispatch() at .github/scripts/security_advisories.py:107-114 POSTs {ref: branch, inputs: {source_sha, lookback_days}} (string values: sha validated, days returned via str()) to /repos/{host}/actions/workflows/sqllens-security-audit.yml/dispatches. This matches the documented GitHub API (ref required, inputs string map, 204 No Content, from my knowledge of the docs; not fetched). GitHub.request line 68 returns None when raw is empty, so a 204 body parses as None.

security_advisories.py:93-106 reads metadata.get('private') (requires is True) and metadata.get('default_branch') (requires non-empty str). GitHub's repository object schema has boolean private and string default_branch. The code also type-checks both, so non-conforming responses raise AuditError.

list_drafts (.github/scripts/security_advisories.py:117-144) validates state==draft and GHSA id format, and requires the Link rel=next path to equal ADVISORIES (/repos/The01Geek/sqllens/security-advisories). It does not validate summary or description (description is read with .get at line 150). Whether GitHub really returns these fields and a next-link path in the /repos/{owner}/{repo} form, rather than the /repositories/{id}/... form it uses for some endpoints, depends on live GitHub API behaviour. I did not run any request against the API and have no captured response, so I cannot settle it from the repository.

security_advisories.py:271-290 sends summary, description, severity, cve_id None, vulnerabilities with package{ecosystem pip,name} and null vulnerable_version_range/patched_versions, start_private_fork False. Per GitHub REST create-repository-advisory docs (from knowledge, not fetched), summary/description/vulnerabilities are required, severity or cvss_vector_string is required, cve_id and the version fields are nullable, start_private_fork is boolean, and the response is an advisory with state draft. The code checks state == draft at line 289.

private_context() (security_advisories.py:298-303) calls require_private with GitHub(GITHUB_TOKEN) for GET /repos/{GITHUB_REPOSITORY} (line 95). Workflow security-audit-private.yml sets permissions contents: read (line 21-22) and passes GITHUB_TOKEN=github.token plus SECURITY_ADVISORY_TOKEN to the prepare/publish steps (62-63, 116-117). Repo metadata GET on the workflow's own repo is allowed by the default token (metadata read is implicit). All advisory operations (list_drafts, publish POST) use client built from SECURITY_ADVISORY_TOKEN (line 381). The dispatch token is a separate dispatch-mode path, not advisory.

security_advisories.py:353-355 appends model=, effort= and schema=<json.dumps(report_schema(sha))> + newline to GITHUB_OUTPUT; json.dumps default is single-line (newlines escaped), so name=value format is valid. Workflow security-audit-private.yml:102,103,111 consume steps.prepare.outputs.model/effort/schema, with schema in single quotes. report_schema (lines 160-190) contains no apostrophes (static strings; analyzed_sha via revision(sha), a validated revision), so single-quote interpolation is not broken.

Line 49 appends AUDIT_CONTEXT_PATH to $GITHUB_ENV in an earlier step of the same job. Line 80 reads ${{ env.AUDIT_CONTEXT_PATH }} in the with.prompt of a later step (audit, line 65). The env context is available in jobs.<job>.steps.with. Values written to GITHUB_ENV are added to the env context for subsequent steps, and step-level expressions are evaluated when that step starts. The value expands $RUNNER_TEMP in the shell before it is written, so it is a literal path. I read the workflow only and did not run it.

security-audit-private.yml:50-57 checks out The01Geek/sqllens main to path: source. The prepare step (l.58-64) has working-directory: source, so git rev-parse HEAD and .prflow/config.json (security_advisories.py:308,312) resolve in that checkout; the HEAD is compared with the dispatched SHA via revision(sha). The analysis prompt (l.73) reads ./source, the same tree. The publish step also uses working-directory: source (l.114).

NORMALIZED (wording-only): .prflow/config.json (head) has claude_model as a string (line 4) but no security_audit key and no workflows.security_audit key (workflows lists only prflow, prflow-review, prflow-retrospective, lines 155-159). So the claim that it contains them is literally wrong. This breaks nothing: security_advisories.py:313-318 and :364 use defaults (effort 'medium', enabled True), the same as the removed jq defaults (`.security_audit.effort // "medium"`, `.workflows.security_audit // true`; diff lines 604-607). The effort value is validated against low/medium/high/max at line 317. The only semantic difference is that jq `//` would turn an explicit false into true, while Python get() honors false. The new docs say to set it to false to disable, so this is intended. No repository rule or contract requires the keys to be present.

Real GitHub.request (.github/scripts/security_advisories.py:45) is request(self, method, route, body=None) and returns (parsed_json_or_None, next_link_or_None) at line 68. FakeGitHub.request (tests/unit/test_private_security_audit.py:97-102) has the same parameters and returns the queued (payload, next_link) tuples; tests supply tuples like ({...}, None). require_private unpacks 'metadata, _' (line 95), consistent with the tuple shape.

security_advisories.py:308 calls check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'], text=True) -> cmd[1]=='rev-parse' returns SHA; line 321-332 calls check_output(['git','log',...], text=True, timeout=30) -> cmd[1]=='log' returns 'synthetic history'. Lambda (test file:368) accepts cmd positional and **kw, so text/timeout kwargs are fine. Test asserts recent_changes == 'synthetic history'.

The YAML 1.1 quirk turns only the `on:` key into boolean True (workflow line 5). The tests never index it. They index jobs.audit.if (workflow line 38, 'github.event.repository.private == true'), top-level permissions (lines 21-22, {contents: read}) and jobs.audit.steps. In the steps, id 'audit' exists (line 66) and has no env key. Its claude_args is a folded `>-` string containing --tools "Read,Glob,Grep", --strict-mcp-config and --setting-sources user (lines 101-112). The first step whose run contains 'publish' is the deliver step (line 113 onward), and its env has AUDIT_CONCLUSION and AUDIT_REPORT_JSON with the exact expected strings (lines 118-119). The earlier steps' run values do not contain 'publish'. Steps with no run key are handled by step.get('run', '').

In .github/scripts/security_advisories.py, publish() (247-295) issues only client.request calls in list_drafts (GET at line 125, with the next link restricted to https://api.github.com and path == ADVISORIES, lines 136-143) and one POST to the collection route ADVISORIES (271-273) that creates an advisory. There is no PATCH/PUT/DELETE and no comment route. The create payload has no state field. Creation is a draft, and the response is rejected unless state == 'draft' (289). Hostile input considered: a pagination Link pointing at a specific advisory route. It is rejected by the path check at 140, and it would only be a GET anyway. Existing drafts are only referenced, never modified.

security_advisories.py:358-408: all of main() runs inside try; the single except Exception handler (402-408) prints only a constant string to stderr, with no exception text, traceback, response body, token or host, and makes no issue/API call. All AuditErrors are constant strings and the GitHub request wrapper re-raises as 'GitHub request failed' (69-70). Subprocess git calls in prepare() (308, 321) run on the public checkout; a CalledProcessError is caught by the handler and its text is not printed. Workflows only invoke the script (security-audit.yml:39, security-audit-private.yml:64,120) and none create issues. The comment describes the handler, which does what it says. Minor caveat: git's own stderr is inherited, but it concerns the public checkout, not private data.

Unset secrets arrive as empty strings. In main() dispatch mode (security_advisories.py:362-378), GitHub('') raises AuditError('Missing credential') at :41-42, before any request. An empty repo would fail repository_name at :74-75. The except at :402-408 prints only a generic message and returns 1. The audit runs only in the private workflow, and the public workflow security-audit.yml has a single dispatch step with no fallback. The only path to exit 0 without dispatching is the explicit security_audit=false config, which is not 'unconfigured'. Hostile input traced: both secrets empty.

In .github/scripts/security_advisories.py, publish() (247-295) makes only GET calls (via list_drafts) and one POST to ADVISORIES to create a draft. No PATCH, PUT or DELETE exists, and nothing in the file changes advisory state, so existing drafts are never edited, closed or published. Dedup uses list_drafts(state=draft) (117-144), draft_index by marker (147-157), and by_id for explicit existing_advisory references (254-260), so it covers current drafts only. This matches docs/internal/security-audits.md:102-104. Absolute-claim trace: an unmarked human draft that a finding does not reference through existing_advisory does produce a second advisory, since by_key and by_id both miss. The doc scopes dedup at lines 99-100 as 'stable finding markers or explicit references', so the claim 'deduplication covers current drafts' is a statement about draft state, not about text-similarity matching. The finding is therefore not a counterexample to the wording, and the never-edited property holds regardless.

security_advisories.py:325-326 git log --max-count=100 and --since=<days> days ago; lookback() line 87-90 enforces 1-90 (called in prepare line 311); line 347-348 raises AuditError if context >256_000 bytes (256 KB decimal) before writing; line 350 os.open mode 0o600 with O_EXCL (new file); workflow security-audit-private.yml:121-123 'Remove private draft context' has if: always(). Overlong context failing in prepare precedes analysis. Hostile input: days=0 or 91 or 3-digit rejected by the regex/range check.

security-audit-private.yml:29-38: privacy job passes github.event.repository.private via env and runs test "$CALLER_PRIVATE" = true; the string compare only succeeds for the exact string 'true', so 'false' and empty both fail. In a reusable workflow the github context is the caller's. The documented caller template (docs/internal/security-audits.md:34) triggers on workflow_dispatch, whose payload includes the repository object with private. Unavailable payload yields an empty string, which fails closed. The audit job's if (line 38) is consistent. I did not run the workflow, so the payload point rests on GitHub's documented event payload and not on a run.

The workflow passes ${{ steps.audit.outputs.structured_output }} straight into AUDIT_REPORT_JSON (security-audit-private.yml:119; security_advisories.py:387 feeds it to publish). security_advisories.py:388 uses os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"] unguarded in publish mode, so it raises KeyError if unset. GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is a default variable the Actions runner sets for every step, and the other workflows in .github/workflows (for example devflow-retrospective.yml:700) use it the same way without defining it. I did not read the security-audit-private.yml step env, so I did not check whether that step overrides the variable.
